taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop drawn on grid edges constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** – Loop where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop alternating between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Suraromu** – Loop passing through numbered gates in order
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop with per-region straight-or-turn constraints on white circles

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop plus placed black cells indicated by directional number clues

#### A3. Path/Connection Drawing
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect islands with bridges (1 or 2) to form a connected network

### B. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells are black (shaded) and which are white.

#### B1. Shading with Number Clues on Grid
- **Nurikabe** – Black cells form connected wall; white islands sized by numbers
- **Kurotto** – Circle numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions
- **Heyawake** – Room-based shading with connectivity and spanning constraints
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns; number clues on black cells
- **Norinori** – Exactly two black cells per region, all as dominoes
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white promontories; no 2×2 black or white
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks
- **Usowan** – Like Heyawake but one clue per room is wrong
- **Tilepaint** – Shade entire tiles to match row/column counts from diagonal clues

#### B2. Shading Forming Specific Shapes
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must be rectangles; white groups must not be rectangles; numbers give area
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; connected, no 2×2, no same-shape adjacency
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms that, when "dropped" by gravity, fill the bottom half

#### B3. Shading by Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no repeats in rows/columns; white connected, no adjacent black

### C. Region Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### C1. Divide into Polyomino Regions
- **Shikaku** – Divide into rectangles, each containing one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide into pentominoes with border-count clues
- **Sashigane** – Divide into L-shaped blocks with circle (knee) and arrow (end) clues
- **Double Choco** – Divide so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions

#### C2. Divide and Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill numbers and implicitly partition into regions of matching size
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1-to-N; arrows indicate largest neighbor direction
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1-to-N; separation constraint on repeated numbers

### D. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### D1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes

#### D2. Number Fill from Clue Lists
- **Nansuke** – Place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-like grid

#### D3. Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or | subject to territory and extension constraints

### E. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves objects within the grid.

#### E1. Placement
- **Akari** (also in B1) – Place light bulbs in white cells
- **Hebi** – Place numbered snakes (1–5) with visibility and adjacency constraints
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths
- **Chained Block** – Determine which cells are black, forming blocks that chain at corners with uniqueness constraints

#### E2. Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

### F. Pencil/Line Drawing (Non-Loop)
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips through cells

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
White cells connected: **Hitori, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Heyawake, Nurimisaki, Usowan**
Black cells connected: **Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin**
Single loop: **Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin**
Connected network: **Hashiwokakero**

### No 2×2 Constraint
No 2×2 black: **Nurikabe, LITS, Sto-stone, Nuritwin**
No 2×2 black or white: **Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu**

### Adjacency Prohibition
No adjacent black cells: **Hitori, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Usowan, Yajilin**
No same-shape adjacency: **LITS, Chained Block**

### Room/Region-Based Clues
**Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Five Cells, Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Double Choco, Sto-stone, Usowan, Dotchi-Loop**

### Directional/Arrow Clues
**Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Sashigane, Evolomino, Pencils, Yosenabe**

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
**Akari** (illumination), **Kurodoko** (white cell count), **Hebi** (snake vision)

---

## III. By Output Type

| Output | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Loop on cell centers** | Masyu, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin |
| **Loop on grid edges** | Slitherlink |
| **Paths/connections** | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Pencils |
| **Binary shading** | Nurikabe, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Norinori, Nurimisaki, LITS, Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Tilepaint, Usowan, Akari, Chained Block |
| **Region boundaries** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Fillomino, Double Choco, Sashigane |
| **Number fill** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Hebi |
| **Symbol fill** | Juosan |
| **Object placement** | Akari (bulbs), Evolomino (squares) |
| **Object movement** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Maze creation** | Nurimeizu |
